boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain University of Michigan-Ann Arbor
boards.description: Under-21-safe late-night destinations with currently published availability; check access restrictions and holiday exceptions before heading out.

cards.title: Pizza House
cards.subtitle: 618 Church St, Ann Arbor
cards.notes: Use the Church Street location for a late meal or delivery. Confirm service details when ordering, especially during campus breaks or severe weather.
cards.short_summary: A Church Street restaurant that publishes daily late dining and delivery availability.
cards.evidence_claim: Pizza House states that its Ann Arbor location offers dine-in or delivery until 4 AM daily.
cards.access_notes: Official site says dine-in or delivery is available until 4 AM daily.

cards.title: BTB Burrito
cards.subtitle: 1140 S University Ave, Ann Arbor
cards.notes: Check the day-specific closing time before walking over. The South University location lists late service on Tuesdays through Saturdays.
cards.short_summary: A South University burrito stop with published late-week hours.
cards.evidence_claim: BTB Burrito lists Ann Arbor hours through 1 AM Tuesday and Wednesday and 2:30 AM Thursday through Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Official hours: Tue–Wed until 1 AM; Thu–Sat until 2:30 AM.

cards.title: New York Pizza Depot
cards.subtitle: 605 E William St, Ann Arbor
cards.notes: Use the restaurant’s own ordering page to confirm the current pickup window and place an order before leaving campus.
cards.short_summary: An East William Street pizza destination with late published pickup hours.
cards.evidence_claim: New York Pizza Depot’s official ordering page lists the Ann Arbor location’s hours as 10:00 AM–2:45 AM.
cards.source_title: New York Pizza Depot — Ann Arbor
cards.access_notes: Official ordering page lists 10:00 AM–2:45 AM; verify holiday changes before going.

cards.title: Fleetwood Diner
cards.subtitle: 300 S Ashley St, Ann Arbor
cards.notes: For a sit-down option, use the walk-in service rather than relying on online-order hours, which the restaurant lists separately.
cards.short_summary: A South Ashley diner whose official ordering site distinguishes 24-hour walk-in access.
cards.evidence_claim: Fleetwood Diner’s official ordering site says it is open 24 hours for walk-ins.
cards.access_notes: Official site states “Open 24 hours for Walk-Ins”; online orders have separate hours.

cards.title: Eigen Café
cards.subtitle: Ford Robotics Building, 2505 Hayward St, Ann Arbor
cards.notes: Head to the Ford Robotics Building for the 24/7 kiosk. Bring an accepted payment method; this is a self-service food and snack stop.
cards.short_summary: Michigan Dining’s 24/7 kiosk in the Ford Robotics Building.
cards.evidence_claim: Michigan Dining lists Eigen Café’s kiosk as open 24/7, from 12:00 AM to 11:59 PM.
cards.access_notes: Official page lists a 24/7 kiosk; Blue Bucks and Dining Dollars are accepted.

cards.title: Blue Market – Munger
cards.subtitle: Munger Graduate Residences, 540 Thompson St, Ann Arbor
cards.notes: Check that you can access Munger before making the trip. Michigan Dining lists this market as a continuous kiosk rather than staffed late service.
cards.short_summary: A Munger market listed by Michigan Dining as a 24/7 kiosk.
cards.evidence_claim: Michigan Dining lists Blue Market – Munger as a 24/7 location, open from 12:00 AM to 11:59 PM.
cards.access_notes: Official directory lists a 24/7 kiosk at Munger; building access may be restricted.

cards.title: PharmFresh
cards.subtitle: College of Pharmacy, 1007 E Huron St, Ann Arbor
cards.notes: Use the College of Pharmacy market kiosk for an overnight snack run. Confirm building access before relying on it after regular hours.
cards.short_summary: A pharmacy-building market that Michigan Dining lists as a 24/7 kiosk.
cards.evidence_claim: Michigan Dining lists PharmFresh as a 24/7 kiosk, open from 12:00 AM to 11:59 PM.
cards.access_notes: Official directory lists a 24/7 kiosk; confirm after-hours building access.

cards.title: Shapiro Undergraduate Library
cards.subtitle: 919 S University Ave, Ann Arbor
cards.notes: Use the library for a late study reset and check its live schedule first. An MCard is required from midnight to 8 AM when it operates overnight.
cards.short_summary: An undergraduate library with published overnight-access guidance.
cards.evidence_claim: The University of Michigan Library states that, when Shapiro is open 24 hours, an MCard is required from midnight to 8 AM.
cards.source_title: Shapiro Library | University of Michigan Library
cards.access_notes: Check the live hours calendar; during 24-hour periods, MCard access is required midnight–8 AM.

cards.title: James and Anne Duderstadt Center
cards.subtitle: 2281 Bonisteel Blvd, Ann Arbor
cards.notes: For North Campus work, arrive before 8 PM or bring your U-M MCard. Verify closures, since the center posts holiday and maintenance exceptions.
cards.short_summary: A North Campus academic center with 24-hour building access when the university is open.
cards.evidence_claim: The Duderstadt Center lists regular hours as 24 hours daily when the university is open, with MCard entry required overnight.
cards.access_notes: Open 24 hours when U-M is open; exterior doors lock 8 PM–8 AM and require a U-M MCard.

cards.entity_name: Walter E. Wilson Student Team Project Center
cards.title: Walter E. Wilson Student Team Project Center
cards.subtitle: 2603 Draper Dr, Ann Arbor
cards.notes: Use this North Campus team-work destination only if you are a student with appropriate access. Its student lounge and project spaces run around the clock.
cards.short_summary: A U-M student project center with 24/7 student accessibility.
cards.evidence_claim: U-M’s tour site says the Wilson Center’s design room, lecture room, and student lounge are accessible to students 24 hours a day, seven days a week.
cards.source_title: Wilson Center | University of Michigan Tour
cards.access_notes: Official tour page says access is 24/7 for students; facility access is intended for student use.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten documented campus places for studying, gathering, making, and taking a break between classes.

cards.title: Central Campus Diag
cards.subtitle: Brick plaza and lawn at the center of Central Campus
cards.notes: Use the paths as a cross-campus reset, then watch for registered organization tables or events. The central brick area, including the M, is reservable.
cards.short_summary: A campus gathering space with room for student-organization events.
cards.evidence_claim: U-M’s Center for Campus Involvement manages the Diag; its policies describe information tables and large events in the central brick space, including the M.
cards.access_notes: Event areas may be reserved; follow posted event and campus-use rules.

cards.title: Eda U. Gerstacker Grove
cards.subtitle: North Campus outdoor gathering space
cards.notes: Build in a few minutes outdoors between North Campus stops. Check the campus calendar for programmed events; organizations and campus partners can reserve the Grove.
cards.short_summary: A managed North Campus green space for outdoor programming.
cards.evidence_claim: The Center for Campus Involvement manages the North Campus Gerstacker Grove, which can be reserved by student organizations and campus partners.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor events require the applicable reservation process.

cards.title: Endover, the rotating Cube
cards.subtitle: Regents’ Plaza on Central Campus
cards.notes: Pause at the kinetic sculpture on a Central Campus walk and see it from several angles. Its axis allows the sculpture to be turned without treating it as a climbing structure.
cards.short_summary: A movable Tony Rosenthal sculpture in Regents’ Plaza.
cards.evidence_claim: Arts at Michigan identifies Endover as The Cube in Regents’ Plaza, created by Tony Rosenthal in 1968, and notes that it can turn on its axis.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor public art; respect the sculpture and surrounding plaza.

cards.title: Maya Lin’s Wave Field
cards.subtitle: North Campus earthwork near the François-Xavier Bagnoud Building
cards.notes: Take the path beside this 90-by-90-foot earth sculpture for a visual change of pace. Keep activity low-impact: U-M does not permit activities on the artwork itself.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor earthwork whose rolling form echoes a natural wave pattern.
cards.evidence_claim: UMMA describes Maya Lin’s 1995 Wave Field as a 90-by-90-foot earth sculpture representing a naturally occurring wave pattern.
cards.source_title: Wave Field | University of Michigan Museum of Art
cards.access_notes: Facilities & Operations states that permitted activities are not allowed on the adjacent Wave Field.

cards.title: Nichols Arboretum
cards.subtitle: 123-acre campus landscape at 1610 Washington Heights
cards.notes: Choose a trail, garden, or river view for a daylight break. Bring water, use the trail map, and leave time to return before sunset.
cards.short_summary: A free campus arboretum with trails, gardens, natural areas, and river access.
cards.evidence_claim: U-M’s botanical gardens identifies Nichols Arboretum as a 123-acre campus landscape with trails, gardens, natural areas, riverfront access, and free admission.
cards.access_notes: Free and open daily from sunrise to sunset; use marked trails and follow visitor guidance.

cards.title: Shapiro Undergraduate Library
cards.subtitle: 919 South University Avenue, Central Campus
cards.notes: Pick a study nook or meet a project group, then use the building’s specialized spaces as needed. Overnight access rules can change, so check current library hours first.
cards.short_summary: A Central Campus library with open study areas, group rooms, and creation spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: The library describes Shapiro as a place to meet for group projects or find a study nook, with study spaces available whenever the building is open.
cards.access_notes: Study spaces are available while the building is open; when Shapiro is open 24 hours, MCard access is required midnight–8 a.m.

cards.title: Michigan Union
cards.subtitle: 530 South State Street, Central Campus
cards.notes: Use its study and meeting areas as a central meetup point, then look for student services or organization resources inside. Check the building page before planning a late visit.
cards.short_summary: A Central Campus union combining study areas, services, eateries, and organization space.
cards.evidence_claim: U-M states that the Michigan Union houses study and meeting spaces, student services, and the IdeaHub for student organizations.
cards.access_notes: Building hours are published by University Unions and may vary by day; some spaces or services have separate access rules.

cards.title: Trotter Multicultural Center
cards.subtitle: 428 South State Street, Central Campus
cards.notes: Stop in for an open study or reflection space, or review the center’s programs and room-request guidance. Respect reservations and the purpose of designated quiet areas.
cards.short_summary: A public-use multicultural center with study, reflection, and reservable spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Trotter says it is open for public use, with spaces for quiet study and reflection; specific spaces can be reserved for events.
cards.source_title: Trotter Multicultural Center Frequently Asked Questions
cards.access_notes: Open public use is subject to current building hours; individual rooms may be reserved.

cards.title: Michigan League Underground
cards.subtitle: Lower level of the Michigan League, 911 North University Avenue
cards.notes: Set up at a table or booth for solo work or a small group. If you need the stage for practice or a performance, contact Conference and Event Services to reserve it.
cards.short_summary: A lower-level study space with tables, booths, and a reservable stage.
cards.evidence_claim: University Unions describes the Michigan League Underground as a place with tables and booths for studying alone or in groups, plus a reservable stage.
cards.access_notes: Stage use requires coordination with Conference and Event Services; follow Michigan League building policies.

cards.title: Pierpont Commons
cards.subtitle: 2101 Bonisteel Boulevard, North Campus
cards.notes: Use the seating and study areas as a practical North Campus meeting point. The building also includes meeting rooms, shops, and services; confirm individual space availability on arrival.
cards.short_summary: North Campus student union with study space, meeting rooms, services, and food options.
cards.evidence_claim: University Unions identifies Pierpont Commons as U-M’s North Campus student union and states that it offers restaurants, meeting rooms, study spaces, shops, and services.
cards.access_notes: Public common areas are subject to building operations; individual shops, services, and meeting rooms have separate availability.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten named, public-facing University of Michigan destinations with documented free admission or free public access.

cards.entity_name: University of Michigan Museum of Art
cards.title: Wander the UMMA galleries
cards.subtitle: 525 S. State St. · Central Campus
cards.notes: Meet at the museum entrance, choose one floor to explore together, and use the gallery map to compare a few works before heading out.
cards.short_summary: A ticket-free art outing with rotating exhibitions and galleries to explore at your own pace.
cards.evidence_claim: UMMA states that tickets are not required and admission is always free for everyone.
cards.source_title: Visit – University of Michigan Museum of Art
cards.access_notes: Public museum; check the visit page for current gallery hours. Photography is allowed without flash or tripods.

cards.title: Browse the Kelsey’s ancient-world galleries
cards.subtitle: 434 S. State St. · Central Campus
cards.notes: Enter through the public Maynard Street entrance, pick a gallery theme, and use the available guide to trade observations as you move through it.
cards.short_summary: A compact archaeology museum where the permanent galleries support an unhurried, no-ticket visit.
cards.evidence_claim: The Kelsey Museum says it is free and open to all, with no tickets or admission fee required.
cards.source_title: Visit – U-M LSA Kelsey Museum of Archaeology
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday–Friday and weekends; closed Mondays and university holidays. Use the public Maynard Street entrance.

cards.entity_name: University of Michigan Museum of Natural History
cards.title: See the natural-history exhibits
cards.subtitle: Biological Sciences Building · 1105 N. University Ave.
cards.notes: Start with a single exhibit hall, set a casual observation challenge, and leave time to look closely at the specimens that catch your group’s eye.
cards.short_summary: Free general museum admission makes this an easy daytime stop for science displays and collections.
cards.evidence_claim: The museum states that general admission is always free for individuals and families.
cards.source_title: University of Michigan Museum of Natural History
cards.access_notes: General admission is free; separately ticketed planetarium or dome programs may have different terms. Check current seasonal hours.

cards.entity_name: Judy and Stanley Frankel Detroit Observatory
cards.title: Visit the Detroit Observatory
cards.subtitle: 1398 E. Ann St. · Hill Area
cards.notes: Check the observatory calendar, arrive through the Observatory Street entrance, and pair a visit with its history-of-astronomy programs or exhibits.
cards.short_summary: A historic campus observatory with free admission and scheduled public programming.
cards.evidence_claim: Detroit Observatory states that admission is always free.
cards.access_notes: Open Thursdays, Fridays, and selected Saturdays; consult the calendar and listed closure dates before visiting.

cards.title: Walk the Matthaei gardens
cards.subtitle: 1800 N. Dixboro Rd. · Northeast Ann Arbor
cards.notes: Choose an outdoor garden or trail loop, slow down at the seasonal plantings, and use the conservatory only when it is open that day.
cards.short_summary: A university botanical garden with outdoor gardens, trails, and a conservatory under free admission.
cards.evidence_claim: Matthaei Botanical Gardens lists free admission.
cards.access_notes: Admission is free. Parking is metered, so arrive by bus, bike, or on foot to keep the outing at zero dollars; conservatory closes Mondays.

cards.title: Take a daylight walk in the Arb
cards.subtitle: 1610 Washington Hts. · Central Campus
cards.notes: Use a marked entrance and trail map, pick a short loop or riverside route, and plan to finish before sunset with a friend or group.
cards.short_summary: A 123-acre campus landscape for trails, gardens, river views, and relaxed outdoor time.
cards.evidence_claim: Nichols Arboretum says it has free admission and is free and open daily from sunrise to sunset.
cards.access_notes: Free daily from sunrise to sunset. Limited parking may be metered; use a daytime visit and stay on established paths.

cards.title: Look through the Hatcher Gallery
cards.subtitle: Harlan Hatcher Graduate Library · Central Campus
cards.notes: Check the library’s current building access, then take a slow pass through the exhibition and choose one detail each person wants to discuss.
cards.short_summary: A free, public art-viewing stop inside Hatcher Graduate Library.
cards.evidence_claim: Michigan Arts describes Hatcher Gallery as free and open to all, during library hours.
cards.access_notes: Free and open to all during library hours; confirm current library access and exhibition availability before going.

cards.title: Drop into the Humanities Gallery
cards.subtitle: 202 S. Thayer St. · Central Campus
cards.notes: Stop by during weekday gallery hours, take in the current installation, and use the posted artist information as a conversation starter.
cards.short_summary: A campus gallery focused on art engaging social justice and humanities themes.
cards.evidence_claim: Michigan Arts identifies the Institute for the Humanities Gallery as free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: Listed gallery hours are Monday–Friday, 9 a.m.–5 p.m.; verify current exhibitions and building access before visiting.

cards.title: See the Lane Hall exhibit
cards.subtitle: 204 S. State St. · Central Campus
cards.notes: Visit during weekday hours, read the exhibit framing before you begin, and leave a few minutes to compare what each person took from the display.
cards.short_summary: A rotating exhibit space centered on gender and sexuality themes.
cards.evidence_claim: The Institute for Research on Women and Gender states that Lane Hall exhibits are free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: Lane Hall – Institute for Research on Women and Gender
cards.access_notes: Free and open to the public Monday–Friday, 9 a.m.–4 p.m.; check the current exhibit listing before visiting.

cards.title: Browse art and science together
cards.subtitle: Dana Building · 440 Church St. · Central Campus
cards.notes: Go during weekday building hours, spend a few minutes with the current work, and talk through the environmental question or material it raises.
cards.short_summary: A university gallery presenting work at the intersection of art and environmental science.
cards.evidence_claim: Michigan Arts lists the Art & Environment Gallery as free and open to the public during building hours.
cards.access_notes: Free and open to the public during building hours, Monday–Friday; verify current building access before visiting.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten University of Michigan Library study environments with documented locations, seating, features, and access considerations.

cards.title: Asia Library Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Hatcher Library North, Floor 4, Room 421
cards.notes: Use the desks, booths, or open tables for quiet work; expect occasional activity when classes or events use adjoining rooms.
cards.short_summary: A quiet, light-filled room combining desks, booths, tables, and the Oka Tadoku Room.
cards.evidence_claim: The room has study desks, booths, open tables, natural light, and a quiet noise level.
cards.source_title: Asia Library Reading Room | University of Michigan Library
cards.access_notes: Located in Hatcher North on floor 4; occasional class or event noise is documented.

cards.title: Hatcher North Stacks Study Tables
cards.subtitle: Hatcher Library North, multiple stack floors
cards.notes: Follow the stack-floor directions to the south-end tables; choose a floor with the seating style that fits your solo or quiet group work.
cards.short_summary: Quiet tables and carrel-style desks distributed across seven stack floors.
cards.evidence_claim: Study seating is available on seven Hatcher North stack floors, near south-end windows, with tables and individual desks varying by floor.
cards.source_title: Hatcher North Stacks Study Tables | University of Michigan Library
cards.access_notes: Use the floor-specific stack entrances and directional markings described by the library.

cards.title: Hatcher South Open Carrels
cards.subtitle: Hatcher Library South, Floors 4 and 5
cards.notes: Settle into an unreserved, windowed carrel for reading or writing; bring headphones if nearby sound would interrupt focused work.
cards.short_summary: Individual desk-and-window cubicles around the Hatcher South stacks.
cards.evidence_claim: These quiet carrels provide a small desk, chair, and window on floors 4 and 5; they are open and not soundproof.
cards.source_title: Hatcher South Open Carrels | University of Michigan Library
cards.access_notes: Open carrels are on floors 4 and 5; floor-3 carrels are separately bookable.

cards.title: Hatcher Floor 6
cards.subtitle: Hatcher Library South, Floor 6
cards.notes: Choose the open seating area for armchairs or divided tables, and use the Special Collections area only during its separate availability window.
cards.short_summary: Quiet sixth-floor seating with campus views, armchairs, tables, and privacy dividers.
cards.evidence_claim: Floor 6 has quiet study seating with views of the Law Quad and Michigan Stadium; the SCRC study space is available weekdays until 5pm.
cards.source_title: Hatcher Floor 6 | University of Michigan Library
cards.access_notes: The Special Collections Research Center portion is available Monday–Friday until 5pm; other seating follows building access.

cards.title: Shapiro Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Shapiro Library, Floor 3, Room 3100
cards.notes: Take a long table for individual focus, or select a smaller table or armchair along the exterior walls for a different posture.
cards.short_summary: A quiet third-floor reading room with padded chairs, lamps, and natural light.
cards.evidence_claim: The quiet room has long tables with padded chairs and lamps, plus smaller tables and armchairs near large windows.
cards.source_title: Shapiro Reading Room | University of Michigan Library
cards.access_notes: Located at the south end of Clark Commons on Shapiro Library’s third floor.

cards.title: Clark Commons Computing Spaces
cards.subtitle: Shapiro Library, Floor 3
cards.notes: Bring a laptop for the extended displays, or use a shared screen and nearby whiteboards when a project needs collaborative setup.
cards.short_summary: Conversational computing seating with external monitors, shared screens, and printing nearby.
cards.evidence_claim: Clark Commons offers extended-monitor bays, shared screens, a computing site with printing, whiteboards, and accessible seating.
cards.source_title: Clark Commons Computing Spaces | University of Michigan Library
cards.access_notes: This is a conversational third-floor Shapiro Library space; it includes computing and printing areas.

cards.entity_name: Taubman Health Sciences Library Study Space
cards.title: Taubman Health Sciences Library Study Space
cards.subtitle: Taubman Health Sciences Library, Floor 4
cards.notes: Use adjustable desks, pod chairs, booths, or table seating for focused work; reserve collaboration needs for the display-equipped west-wall areas.
cards.short_summary: A quiet, light-filled library space with varied seating, computing, and collaboration displays.
cards.evidence_claim: The fourth-floor space offers adjustable desks, pod chairs, booths, tables, external monitors, and three collaboration areas.
cards.source_title: Taubman Health Sciences Library Study Space | University of Michigan Library
cards.access_notes: Extended hours require MCard entry and are limited to specified medical and graduate student populations.

cards.entity_name: Art, Architecture, and Engineering Library Floor 2 Stacks Spaces
cards.title: AAEL Floor 2 Stacks Spaces
cards.subtitle: Art, Architecture, and Engineering Library, Floor 2
cards.notes: Head through the northeast double doors from the lobby, then choose window counters, individual desks, large tables, or corner armchairs.
cards.short_summary: Quiet second-floor stacks seating inside the Duderstadt Center with several work surfaces.
cards.evidence_claim: The quiet stacks area includes bar-height window counters, individual desks, large tables, corner armchairs, natural light, and wheelchair access.
cards.source_title: Art, Architecture, and Engineering Library Floor 2 Stacks Spaces | University of Michigan Library
cards.access_notes: Enter the Duderstadt Center’s floor 2, then pass from lobby spaces through the northeast double doors.

cards.title: Fine Arts Library Floor 2
cards.subtitle: Fine Arts Library, Tappan Hall, Floor 2
cards.notes: Enter through Tappan Hall’s second-floor doors and choose a large wood table or a deeper-in-the-stacks table; keep food wrapped and drinks covered.
cards.short_summary: A quiet, high-ceilinged, book-lined room with large wood tables and window light.
cards.evidence_claim: The second floor has quiet study space with large wooden tables, book stacks, natural light, and restrictions to covered drinks and wrapped food.
cards.source_title: Fine Arts Library Floor 2 | University of Michigan Library
cards.access_notes: Enter via Tappan Hall’s second floor; only covered drinks and wrapped food are permitted.

cards.title: Music Library Floors 3 and 4
cards.subtitle: Music Library, Floors 3 and 4
cards.notes: Use floor 3 for window tables or armchair clusters, and plan for stairs to floor 4 unless staff can assist with the elevator.
cards.short_summary: Quiet, airy North Campus study floors with tables, armchairs, and wooded views.
cards.evidence_claim: All Music Library study space is on floors 3 and 4, with natural light, tables, armchairs, and wheelchair accessibility.
cards.source_title: Music Library Floors 3 and 4 | University of Michigan Library
cards.access_notes: Floor-4 primary access is by stairs; request staff help at the Information Services Desk for elevator use. Covered drinks and small snacks only.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented University of Michigan traditions, from the Diag’s bronze M to game-day rituals at Michigan Stadium.

cards.title: Avoid the bronze M
cards.subtitle: The Diag
cards.notes: Find the bronze block M embedded in the Diag, photograph it from the walkway, and treat the exam-failure warning as campus folklore rather than fact.
cards.short_summary: A long-running superstition attached to a very visible campus marker.
cards.evidence_claim: LSA identifies not stepping on the bronze “M” in the Diag as a University of Michigan student superstition.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus walkway; view it without blocking pedestrian traffic.

cards.title: Form the incoming-class Block M
cards.subtitle: Michigan Stadium
cards.notes: If you are an incoming student, follow New Student Programs instructions for the stadium field photo and wear the requested maize shirt.
cards.short_summary: The incoming class assembles on the Big House field to create a giant M.
cards.evidence_claim: U-M New Student Programs calls the Block M photo a Michigan tradition that brings the entire incoming class together on the Michigan Stadium field.
cards.access_notes: Scheduled welcome-program activity for incoming students; follow registration and entry instructions.

cards.title: Begin with Convocation
cards.subtitle: Crisler Center
cards.notes: Check the welcome schedule before arrival, then join the official academic welcome and listen for remarks from campus and student leaders.
cards.short_summary: A formal welcome that marks the start of undergraduate study at Michigan.
cards.evidence_claim: New Student Programs describes New Student Convocation as a Michigan tradition and the official academic welcome for incoming undergraduates.
cards.access_notes: Scheduled welcome-program activity; consult the current event listing for entry details.

cards.title: Learn the chants before kickoff
cards.subtitle: Michigan Stadium
cards.notes: Use the official welcome calendar to confirm the date, bring your MCard if required, and learn the athletics chants and cheers in the stadium.
cards.short_summary: A welcome-week rally devoted to Michigan athletics songs, chants, and cheers.
cards.evidence_claim: The 2026 Student Kick-off Rally listing invites students to learn Michigan Athletics’ time-honored traditions, chants, and cheers.
cards.access_notes: The current listing specifies MCard entry for students; verify the event’s current requirements.

cards.entity_name: Go Blue M Club Supports You Banner
cards.title: Watch the team touch the banner
cards.subtitle: Michigan Stadium tunnel entrance
cards.notes: At a football game, watch the pregame entrance from your assigned area as players run from the tunnel and leap for the banner.
cards.short_summary: Michigan football players leap to touch a 30-foot banner on their way to the field.
cards.evidence_claim: Michigan Athletics says players have raced from the tunnel and leapt to touch the “Go Blue M Club Supports You” banner as part of the tradition since 1962.
cards.source_title: Go Blue M Club Supports You
cards.access_notes: Occurs during football pregame; stadium access and game admission rules apply.

cards.title: Listen for “The Victors”
cards.subtitle: Michigan athletics and marching-band tradition
cards.notes: Listen for the fight song at a sanctioned athletics or band event, and use an official song sheet if you want to follow along.
cards.short_summary: The university fight song grew from an 1898 football moment and remains central to Michigan spirit.
cards.evidence_claim: The U-M Library’s encyclopedic survey says Louis Elbel wrote “The Victors” after Michigan’s 1898 Chicago game and calls it one of Michigan’s greatest songs.
cards.source_title: The University of Michigan, an Encyclopedic Survey
cards.access_notes: Hear it at scheduled public athletic and marching-band appearances; access varies by event.

cards.title: Catch pregame with the band
cards.subtitle: Michigan Stadium
cards.notes: Arrive before football kickoff if your ticket permits, then watch the Marching Band’s pregame performance and listen for “The Victors.”
cards.short_summary: The marching band anchors the sound and ceremony of Michigan football pregame.
cards.evidence_claim: Michigan Athletics describes the football team’s banner entrance as a pregame tradition performed while the Marching Band plays “The Victors.”
cards.source_title: Go Blue M Club Supports You
cards.access_notes: Occurs before football kickoff; stadium access and game admission rules apply.

cards.title: See the Rock’s newest layer
cards.subtitle: Hill Street and Washtenaw Avenue
cards.notes: Walk past the painted boulder, photograph its current message from the sidewalk, and seek university permission before adding any paint yourself.
cards.short_summary: Student organizations have repeatedly transformed a Washington memorial boulder into a changing public canvas.
cards.evidence_claim: U-M’s Center for Academic Innovation calls painting the Rock at Hill Street and Washtenaw a well-established tradition among student organizations.
cards.source_title: Creating Community for the Academic Innovation Summer Fellows
cards.access_notes: Visible from public sidewalks; do not paint or alter the memorial without applicable authorization.

cards.title: Read the Rock’s backstory
cards.subtitle: Hill Street and Washtenaw Avenue
cards.notes: Pair a sidewalk view of the boulder with Bentley’s account of its 1932 installation and the painted practice that continued despite a later warning sign.
cards.short_summary: A 1932 Washington memorial became a persistent, evolving Michigan student tradition.
cards.evidence_claim: Bentley Historical Library reports that painting the Rock began likely in the mid-1950s and that the tradition continues today.
cards.access_notes: View from the public right-of-way and respect the memorial, nearby traffic, and any posted rules.

cards.title: Spot the winged helmet
cards.subtitle: Michigan football
cards.notes: Look for the helmet during an official football event or in university athletics materials, and use the alumni timeline for its 1938 debut context.
cards.short_summary: The distinctive football helmet has been part of Michigan’s visual identity since Fritz Crisler’s arrival.
cards.evidence_claim: The U-M Alumni Association says Coach Fritz Crisler’s 1938 arrival brought the debut of the winged helmet.
cards.access_notes: See it at official football events or through publicly available university athletics coverage.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at University of Michigan-Ann Arbor, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A walkable, under-21-safe first-weekend sequence connecting Central Campus and downtown Ann Arbor through public places and recurring activities.

cards.title: Start at the Michigan Union
cards.subtitle: Friday arrival · Central Campus
cards.notes: Use the Union as a first indoor waypoint: orient yourself, browse the historic halls, and find the Campus Information Center before heading out.
cards.short_summary: A central gathering place with student services, eateries, and study space.
cards.evidence_claim: The Michigan Union at 530 S. State Street has study and meeting spaces, eateries, shops, student services, and the IdeaHub.
cards.access_notes: University Unions lists building hours daily; check the page for holiday or break adjustments.

cards.title: Walk the Diag
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · Central Campus
cards.notes: Cross the Diag slowly and use its landmarks to build your campus bearings; the Block M, libraries, and Angell Hall are all on this route.
cards.short_summary: The heart of Central Campus and a practical landmark walk.
cards.evidence_claim: U-M’s tour identifies the Diag as Central Campus’s heart, with the Block M and nearby Hatcher, Shapiro, Angell, and other buildings.
cards.access_notes: An outdoor campus route; follow posted campus guidance and use accessible paths as needed.

cards.title: Pause at the Law Quad
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · South State Street
cards.notes: Take in the courtyard and Tudor Gothic exterior, then continue toward State Street; treat study areas as active academic spaces and keep the visit quiet.
cards.short_summary: A historic academic quadrangle near UMMA and Central Campus.
cards.evidence_claim: U-M describes the Law Quad at 625 S. State Street as Tudor Gothic and notes that students use its spaces to relax and study.
cards.access_notes: The quad contains active law-school spaces; respect posted access and quiet-study expectations.

cards.entity_name: University of Michigan Museum of Art
cards.title: See art at UMMA
cards.subtitle: Friday evening · 525 S. State Street
cards.notes: Choose a gallery or two instead of rushing the building. Check in on arrival, use the museum map, and keep flash off if you take photos.
cards.short_summary: A free art museum visit steps from the Union and Law Quad.
cards.evidence_claim: UMMA states that admission is always free, tickets are not required, and non-flash photography is allowed in the galleries.
cards.source_title: Visit — University of Michigan Museum of Art
cards.access_notes: Free admission; gallery hours vary by day and the museum is closed Mondays, so verify the visit page before going.

cards.title: Find the Michigan League fountain
cards.subtitle: Friday evening · North Central Campus
cards.notes: Walk past the stained glass and courtyard, then find the Sunday Morning in Deep Waters fountain outside for a clear campus photo landmark.
cards.short_summary: A historic student union with distinctive architecture and an outdoor fountain.
cards.evidence_claim: University Unions identifies the Michigan League as a student union known for historic architecture, stained glass, courtyard garden, and its front fountain.
cards.access_notes: Building hours differ by day; check the official page before planning an indoor stop.

cards.title: Browse the Saturday market
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning · 315 Detroit Street
cards.notes: Make this an early Saturday stop. Browse the farm, food, and artisan stalls, and bring a payment method only if you plan to buy something.
cards.short_summary: A recurring Saturday market near Kerrytown with seasonal vendors.
cards.evidence_claim: The City lists Saturday market hours year-round at 315 Detroit Street, with Wednesday markets also running May through December.
cards.source_title: Ann Arbor Farmers Market — City of Ann Arbor
cards.access_notes: Saturday hours are 8 a.m.–3 p.m. January–April and 7 a.m.–3 p.m. May–December; purchases are optional.

cards.title: Take a downtown library break
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · Fifth and William
cards.notes: Use the Downtown Library for a reset: browse the shelves, look for current exhibits, or settle into one of the public seating areas before dinner.
cards.short_summary: A public downtown stop with collections, seating, exhibits, and study rooms.
cards.evidence_claim: AADL lists the Downtown Library at 343 South Fifth Avenue and says all locations are open for browsing, seating, checkout, and phone calls daily.
cards.source_title: Locations & Hours — Ann Arbor District Library
cards.access_notes: Listed hours are 10 a.m.–8 p.m. daily, except closures; verify the current closures page before visiting.

cards.entity_name: University of Michigan Museum of Natural History
cards.title: Meet the dinosaurs at UMMNH
cards.subtitle: Sunday morning · Biological Sciences Building
cards.notes: Plan a self-guided loop through the exhibits, then check the museum map for temporary closures before deciding whether to add a planetarium program.
cards.short_summary: A free natural-history museum with exhibits ranging from molecules to dinosaurs.
cards.evidence_claim: The museum says individual and family admission is free and describes exhibits spanning molecules, dinosaurs, a planetarium, and science demonstrations.
cards.source_title: Visitor Information — U-M Museum of Natural History
cards.access_notes: Free for individuals and families; September–May hours are Tuesday–Sunday, 10 a.m.–4 p.m., with Monday closure.

cards.title: Walk the Arb trails
cards.subtitle: Sunday afternoon · 1610 Washington Heights
cards.notes: Choose one trail or garden area and carry water. Start with a trail map at an entrance, stay on marked paths, and leave time to return before sunset.
cards.short_summary: A 123-acre campus landscape of trails, gardens, river access, and seasonal blooms.
cards.evidence_claim: U-M’s Nichols Arboretum page describes a 123-acre landscape with trails, gardens, natural areas, riverfront access, and free daily admission.
cards.source_title: Nichols Arboretum — Matthaei Botanical Gardens & Nichols Arboretum
cards.access_notes: Free and open daily from sunrise to sunset; use the official trail map and observe posted conditions.

cards.title: Finish along the Huron River
cards.subtitle: Sunday afternoon · 301 E. Huron Street
cards.notes: Take the riverside paths or the Argo Pond walk for a final outdoor loop. Stay on open trails, observe park rules, and avoid river activity in unsafe conditions.
cards.short_summary: A 22-acre Huron River park with trails, paths, and the Argo Cascades.
cards.evidence_claim: The City describes Argo as a 22-acre riverfront park and nature area with trails, paths, the Argo Pond walk, and the nine-drop Argo Cascades.
cards.source_title: Argo Park & Nature Area — City of Ann Arbor
cards.access_notes: Park hours are 6 a.m.–10 p.m. The City prohibits alcohol and requires dogs to be leashed; heed posted closures and river advisories.
